|---|---|---|

| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu (90%) | Classes not separable |

| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models pick different classes |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 4) · ↓ invasive · Low score here, lowering invasive association [F2] · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 1, 9, 11) · ↓ invasive · High score; fits in situ or atypical lesion (12/20 spot check) [F3] · Weak
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 0, 4) · ↓ invasive · High score, but spot check failed (0/20) [F4] · Unreliable
- **Tumor cell fraction and density** (regions 6, 9, 10) · context · 91% neoplastic nuclei, highest in reference set [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Faithful to the classifier; deleting top 3 regions beats random by 0.54 logit (CI 0.47–0.60).
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI spans 0 (−0.005 to 0.007), so unproven; this case leans on Unreliable normal lobules.

## Could be wrong if
- Image is atypical versus training data (OOD 88th percentile), so probabilities may be off.
- Dense neoplastic nuclei (91%) mean in situ disease, not benign.

## Check on the slide
1. **6, 9, 10**: confirm nuclei are neoplastic; look for duct-confined atypia.
2. **10**: highest per-region invasive probability (19%); look for stromal invasion.
3. **1, 9, 11**: separate usual hyperplasia from atypia; CK5/6 and ER are drafted.
